readings: Sets for every bootstrap are KIT parameter sets (one protocol at one temperature) and Sandia groups (chemistry, ambient, window, rates), as D74 reads the brief's 'resampling protocols, not pairs'; the pooled draws are stratified (KIT sets and Sandia groups drawn separately). Resampling protocols instead is reported as a sensitivity (out/B.json, 'sens ... protocol clusters').

The 25 C band is the one whose archived interval (hi - lo) is narrower, protocol by protocol for KIT and chemistry by chemistry for Sandia; a lever that is not determinable has no interval and cannot be the narrower (LFP 25 C goes to 15 to 25 C). Sandia 15 C sets take the 15 to 25 C lever and 35 C sets the 25 to 35 C lever.
Every Sandia pair takes its chemistry's registered 1C lever for its band, the 2C and 3C groups included (D72's literal wording); the secondary 2C series is not used.
KIT tie: |L_warm - L_cool| strictly below the larger res90_efc of the two cells. Sandia tie: below_resolution as archived.

Orientation: KIT as archived (warm = higher T_C, checked against stage2_cells.csv); Sandia by the larger rise (measure (a)) and, for the measure (b) bracket, by the larger rest temperature; no exact tie occurs in either.
d = ln(L_warm / L_cool) as the log of the ratio; p = -s dT with s in natural-log units per K.

Untied bracket: the dataset restricted to its untied pairs, the bootstrap drawing the sets that hold one (2 KIT sets); drawing all 36 KIT sets (sets without an untied pair adding nothing, empty draws left out and counted) gives the same interval and is reported as a sensitivity. Pooled untied equals KIT untied (Sandia has no untied scored pair).

B4's interval uses B1's draws: in each draw beta is refitted over the drawn pairs, the residuals of those pairs give sd* = sqrt(sum r^2 / (n* - 1)) with n* the draw's pair count. 'Lies inside that interval' is read as the closed interval.
B2 for the 0 C KIT sets uses the same bootstrap over its 12 sets.
B3 is computed for KIT, Sandia and pooled, each over all scored pairs and per band; a pair with d = 0 or p = 0 would be left out (none is).
Extras not named in D74, computed from the same draws and labelled so: beta and B4 per band (D76 mentions 'B1 to B4 per dataset and band'), s_w over a whole dataset.

C1 calculation: noncentral t with df n - 1 and nc = |s| sqrt(sum dT^2) / sd(e), both tails, from scipy.stats.nct directly; where scipy returns nan for the lower tail the quadrature value is used (this happened only at Brent's trial points nc = 11.8 and 23.7, never at a reported value). Brent's method on nc, then |s| = nc sd(e) / sqrt(sum dT^2).

C1 simulation: one set of 10,000 datasets per case and shape; rejection |t| > t_0.975(n - 1); 'reaches 0.80' as simulated power >= 0.80; bisection on |s| from [0, 2 s_calc] (doubling if needed) until hi - lo <= 1e-6 hi, the reported value being hi; the exact step of the simulated power is reported beside. The random sign is +1 or -1 with probability 1/2 each.
The normal-e simulation uses the registered shape's sd(e); the normal-shape calculation uses m sqrt(pi / 2).
Shared-cell F = (sum over cells of w^2) / (2 sum over pairs of dT^2) per selection; the pooled F sums over the cells of both datasets; the shared-cell line keeps df = n - 1.
C2's simulated power is C1's per-band simulation (the same 10,000 datasets) evaluated at the band's median |s|.

C2's simulated n follows Stage 4's bisection (2 first; then lo = 2, hi = max(4 n_calc, 3), doubling while hi fails), fresh 10,000 datasets at each n tried, each drawing n dT values with replacement from the band's observed dT and e from the registered shape.
C2 is computed for every dataset, band and floor; D75 names KIT under the KIT floor and Sandia and pooled under both floors; KIT under the Geslin floor is an extra.

P6 compares the detectable |s| with the full-precision band medians (1.302942364773262 and 3.5800471015633453 % per K), 'exceeds' strict. P1 and P2 read the interval as closed; P7 as width ratio >= 2; P8 as upper end <= 3.

V3: D77's 'first Sandia NMC pair at 25 C in the order of results/stage3_pairs.csv' is literally the 0-100 %, 0.5/0.5C pair, which has no measure (a) and is not scored; its parenthesis names the 0-100 %, 0.5/1C pair of cells a and b, which is the one computed.

flags: Ties: by D72's rule 140 of the 142 KIT pairs (104 of the 106 scored) are ties, so the KIT untied bracket holds two pairs (P049-3/P049-2 and P052-3/P052-1, both 25 C, warm band) in two sets and no cold pair; its numbers (beta -88.2, s_w 170 % per K, residual sd 0.456) carry no information, and the pooled untied bracket is the same two pairs. D72 reports the empty Sandia bracket but not the near-empty KIT one.

Monte Carlo noise in the intervals: this run's KIT beta interval [-1.913, 1.427] lies 2.4 and 2.0 Monte Carlo sd from the mean of 200 replicate 10,000-draw bootstraps [-2.015, 1.344] (end sd 0.043, 0.042); 1,000,000 draws give [-2.032, 1.343]. The pooled lower end -0.557 lies 2.2 sd from its replicate mean -0.511. The seed was fixed before the run and is kept; the pipeline's intervals should be compared within several Monte Carlo sd, not to rounding. P1, P2 and P8 hold in all 200 replicates and at 1,000,000 draws.

Pooled warm s_w: this run's interval [-7.108, -0.030] % per K excludes zero, but 65.5% of the replicates and the 1,000,000-draw interval [-7.106, 0.031] include it: any statement that the pooled warm within-set lever is negative rests on Monte Carlo noise (unscored).

B4, pooled against the KIT floor: the interval's lower end 0.1056 lies 0.0014 above sd(e) = 0.10413, so the pooled noise is recorded as not the KIT floor; stable over Monte Carlo (no replicate includes it; 1,000,000 draws give 0.1057) but a margin of 1.4 %. KIT and Sandia include the KIT floor's sd(e) and exclude Geslin's in every replicate. For KIT the comparison is partly circular (D74): the KIT floor comes from cells 1 and 2 of these same sets.

P3 fails on the point estimate: the KIT warm s_w is -5.19 % per K [-16.0, 8.2]. In the same band the registered per-band sign test (unscored) gives 24 of 70 agreeing, two-sided p = 0.0115, and the per-band beta (an extra, not a B1 quantity) is -7.75 [-17.82, -1.95], excluding both 0 and 1: the KIT beta near zero (-0.086) mixes a negative warm band with a cold band at 0.32 [-0.78, 2.65].
P4 holds on a point estimate of -0.79 % per K whose interval [-9.3, 4.0] spans zero widely: deterministic, but the sign carries little information.

P7 fails by a wide margin (width ratio 0.954; replicate means 3.223 and 3.359; 1,000,000 draws 0.953): the Sandia swing differences (dT rms 1.54 K against 0.44 K for KIT) give its 56 pairs more leverage than KIT's 106; the ties the prediction names do not decide the width.

Sandia without the NCA 15 C 1C pair (bracket): beta 1.809 [0.117, 2.832] excludes zero in every replicate (lower end sd 0.025; 1,000,000 draws 0.116), against 1.550 [-0.707, 2.482] with it: one pair whose cell b sensor did not follow the cell (dT 3.98 K, the largest in its band) moves the Sandia interval off zero. Unscored.
Sandia measure (b) orients 21 of the 56 pairs the other way from measure (a); beta 0.698 [-2.256, 2.646].

Pooling mixes two temperature measures: KIT dT is the difference of mean cell temperatures, Sandia dT the difference of within-cycle swings (D43, D72); and the Sandia 2C and 3C groups carry the 1C lever (D72), though Stage 3's secondary 2C levers differ (NCA 25 to 35 C +1.30 against -2.04 % per K at 1C; NMC -7.14 against -2.44).

V4 (C1): within 5 % in 19 of 20 cases with this run's seeds; it fails in Sandia cold | Geslin (-0.0617; passes in 5% of 20 replicate simulations, mean -0.0590). Seed-dependent V4 verdicts (replicate pass share strictly between 0 and 1): Sandia warm | Geslin (replicate pass share 0.95, mean -0.0395); Sandia cold | Geslin (replicate pass share 0.05, mean -0.0590); Sandia cold | KIT (replicate pass share 0.75, mean -0.0474). P6's case passes in every replicate.

C1's calculation keeps df = n - 1 and independent pairs, while the pairs of a set share cells (F = 1.5000 KIT, 1.7240 Sandia, 1.6944 pooled); the shared-cell line raises KIT's detectable |s| to 8.034 % per K, still at df = n - 1.

The named cases agree closely: KIT warm 4147 against 4221 (5 replicates [4176, 4196, 4242, 4230, 4203]), KIT cold 198 against 205 (5 replicates [204, 203, 207, 204, 205]).

Influence (checker's leave-one-set-out sensitivity, out/influence.json): one set carries most of each fit. KIT P036 (10 C, 10-100 1.67/1.00C, lever -11.59 % per K) holds 52% of KIT's sum of p^2; without it KIT beta is -0.373 [-2.91, 2.01]. Sandia NMC 25 C 0-100 0.5/3C (a 3C group carrying the 1C lever; its cell c has the smallest swing, 6.0 K against 10.1 to 11.3 K, and the shortest life) holds 57% of Sandia's and 41% of the pooled sum of p^2 (Sandia as a whole 72 %); without it Sandia beta is 0.679 [-1.42, 2.94] and pooled 0.320 [-0.86, 1.56], against 1.550 and 1.096 with it. No verdict changes (P7's ratio would be about 1.3), but the Sandia and pooled point values describe one group more than the dataset.
